shorts.title: What you will learn: Pass by value
shorts.hook: A function changes a copy, not your variable.
shorts.script: A function changes a copy, not your variable. Today we meet a surprise. A function can change its input, and your variable still stays the same. When you pass a value to a function, C plus plus makes a copy. The function works on the copy. The original variable never changes. This is called pass by value. To send a result out, use return. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Pass by value.

shorts.script: When you pass a value to a function, C plus plus makes a copy. The function works on the copy. The original variable never changes. This is called pass by value. To send a result out, use return. Think of a photocopy. You can scribble on the copy, and the original stays clean. Number is ten. We call double it with number. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: The function swaps a and b.
shorts.script: The function swaps a and b. It uses a helper box t. Main calls it with x and y. The function swaps only its copies. So x is still one, and y is still two. We need another way to change the originals. That is the next episode. The program prints one and two. Nothing was swapped. Arguments are copied into the parameters. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Expecting the original to change
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in pass by value?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in pass by value? Bug of the Day. Add tax should raise the price to one hundred and five. But the program prints one hundred. The function changed only a copy. Return the new price, and store it in the variable. Now the answer is right. The function changes its own copy of price, and then the copy disappears. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Expecting the original to change.
